sections.title: Why this module matters
sections.body: Engineering practices interview questions test whether you operate as a senior engineer outside the IDE — running effective code reviews, writing Architecture Decision Records (ADRs), managing technical debt strategically, building knowledge-sharing culture, mentoring junior engineers, leading cross-team initiatives, and the technical-leadership questions that come up at staff and principal level ("how would you approach the first 90 days on a team with high tech debt?"). Pair this with the Behavioral page for the full senior-interview narrative surface.

sections.title: Mental model
sections.body:
Senior engineering = **what you do outside the IDE**.

- **Code review** — catch design issues, not bracket placement; be kind, be specific.
- **ADRs** — capture *why*, not just *what*. Future-you will thank you.
- **Tech debt** — log it as a backlog item, link to symptoms; don't moralise.
- **Mentoring** — pair on hard tickets, leave artefacts (docs, recordings).
- **Cross-team** — write the doc *before* the meeting.

sections.title: Must-know concepts
sections.body:

sections.title: Likely interview hooks
sections.body:
- **"How do you handle disagreement in code review?"** — surface the underlying principle, ask, agree.
- **"How would you onboard onto a high-debt team?"** — listen 30 days, write the map, fix one thing visibly.
- **"How do you prioritise tech debt?"** — by *cost of carry* + risk, not aesthetics.
- **"How do you mentor?"** — observable goals, weekly checkpoints, public credit.
- **"How do you write ADRs?"** — context, decision, consequences; one page max.

sections.title: Speaking template
sections.body: > *"My approach is <listen → map → fix one>. I'd write an ADR for the call, run the change through code review with a focus on <design / observability / failure modes>, and follow up with a 1-pager so the team can refer back."*
